page: Amazon Web Services c6g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv8-based Neoverse-N1 architecture, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor, includes a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, and does not feature local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server exhibits strong multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and strong software compilation speeds with Clang, alongside strong static web serving throughput and cached read-only memory bandwidth. However, single-core performance is weaker, as evidenced by lower scores in single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core tests. Large-block memory bandwidth and Passmark database operations fall within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture delivers high resource density with 64 dedicated physical cores, offering a favorable performance-per-resource profile for highly parallelized workloads. The server is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and containerized microservices. It is less suited for single-threaded processing or large-scale LLM inference, where text generation and large-model prompt processing benchmarks show weak performance.
